elements.description:
Brace initializer for an EngineWindowEvent declaration, with zeroed event data.
Each argument is evaluated once. Available with the same name in C and C++.
elements.examples: EngineWindowEvent event = ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_INITIALIZER(window, ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_FOCUS_GAINED);
elements.name: ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_INITIALIZER

elements.description:
Brace initializer for an EngineWindowEvent declaration with type ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_RESIZED.
Each argument is evaluated once. Available with the same name in C and C++.
elements.examples: EngineWindowEvent event = ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_RESIZED_INITIALIZER(window, 800, 600);
elements.name: ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_RESIZED_INITIALIZER

elements.description:
Payload for ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT with data_size equal to sizeof(EngineWindowEvent).
m_Type selects the valid union member. Only ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_RESIZED has
event-specific data: m_Data.m_Resized contains the physical framebuffer dimensions.
Do not read that member for other notification types.
Resize delivery follows the existing window state updates and notifications,
once per native resize callback with no initial-size replay. Window events may
arrive before engine Initialize; m_Window can be null during early startup.
Obtain the source engine from the extension context registry using ENGINE_CONTEXT_NAME.

members.doc: borrowed source window, or null if not yet available
members.name: m_Window

members.doc: physical framebuffer width; valid only for ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_RESIZED
members.name: m_Data.m_Resized.m_Width

members.doc: physical framebuffer height; valid only for ENGINE_WINDOW_EVENT_RESIZED
members.name: m_Data.m_Resized.m_Height

info.description:
Built-in event identifiers and payloads published through the generic extension
event transport in `<dmsdk/extension/extension.h>`. Custom events may use
their own identifiers and payloads without central registration.

Payloads and their handles are borrowed for the synchronous callback. Obtain
the source engine from the callback registry using ENGINE_CONTEXT_NAME.
Get the registry with ExtensionParamsGetContextRegistry, then use ContextRegistryGet
and cast the result to HEngine. Use EngineGetWindow for its current window.
Window payloads identify the source window directly. A window
handle may be null during early startup or failure cleanup.
Window notifications retain the backend focus/minimize semantics. Minimization
is distinct from hide/show visibility; platform callback availability is unchanged.
